title: Cuts and Wounds
shortDescription: Basic first-aid steps for minor cuts and wounds.
whenToGetHelp: Seek professional medical care if the wound is deep, heavily bleeding, caused by a serious object, or shows signs of infection.
steps: Wash your hands before touching the wound.
Apply gentle pressure with clean gauze or cloth to control bleeding.
Rinse the wound gently with clean running water.
Clean around the wound with soap and water.
Cover the wound with a clean dressing or bandage.
Change the dressing when it becomes dirty or wet.
Monitor the wound for increasing redness, swelling, pain, warmth, or discharge.

title: Minor Burns
shortDescription: Basic first-aid information for minor thermal burns.
whenToGetHelp: Seek medical attention for extensive, deep, electrical, chemical, facial, genital, or major burns.
steps: Move away from the source of the burn.
Cool the affected area with cool running water.
Continue cooling the area for several minutes.
Remove jewelry or tight items near the burn if they are not stuck to the skin.
Cover the burn loosely with a clean, non-stick dressing.
Do not break blisters.
Do not apply butter, oil, toothpaste, or other household substances to the burn.

title: Nosebleeds
shortDescription: What to do when someone experiences a nosebleed.
whenToGetHelp: Seek medical attention if bleeding is severe, follows a significant injury, causes difficulty breathing, or does not stop after sustained pressure.
steps: Sit upright and remain calm.
Lean slightly forward rather than backward.
Pinch the soft part of the nose firmly.
Maintain continuous pressure for several minutes.
Breathe through the mouth while holding pressure.
Avoid blowing or picking the nose immediately after the bleeding stops.
Seek professional help if the bleeding continues or appears severe.

title: Sprains
shortDescription: Basic first-aid information for suspected minor sprains.
whenToGetHelp: Seek medical assessment when there is severe pain, major swelling, deformity, inability to use the affected limb, numbness, or suspected fracture.
steps: Stop the activity and protect the injured area.
Rest the affected joint.
Apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth for short periods.
Use gentle compression if appropriate and comfortable.
Elevate the affected limb when possible.
Avoid activities that increase pain or swelling.
Seek professional assessment if symptoms are severe or do not improve.

title: Fainting
shortDescription: Basic first-aid response when someone loses consciousness briefly.
whenToGetHelp: Seek emergency medical help if the person does not quickly regain consciousness, has difficulty breathing, has a seizure, suffered a significant injury, or has concerning symptoms.
steps: Check that the area is safe.
Check whether the person responds to you.
If they are breathing and there is no immediate danger, help them lie down safely.
Avoid giving food or drink while the person is unconscious.
Monitor their breathing and responsiveness.
Allow the person to recover gradually.
Seek medical help when the cause is unknown, the episode is recurrent, or concerning symptoms are present.

title: Choking
shortDescription: Emergency information for a person who may be choking.
whenToGetHelp: Choking that prevents normal breathing is a medical emergency. Contact your local emergency service immediately.
steps: Ask the person if they are choking and determine whether they can cough or speak.
If they can cough forcefully, encourage them to continue coughing.
If they cannot breathe, speak, or cough effectively, treat the situation as an emergency.
Call your local emergency service or have someone call while first aid is provided.
Use the appropriate choking first-aid technique for the person's age and condition.
If the person becomes unresponsive, begin appropriate CPR procedures and follow emergency-dispatch instructions.
After a serious choking episode, medical evaluation may be necessary.
